term: fallible process-type reliability and conditional reliability
definition: Reliability is the truth-conducive tendency of a cognitive process-type; conditional reliability evaluates output truth given true belief-inputs. Neither requires that every token output be true. The recursive justification clause additionally requires justified input beliefs, and the paper leaves the threshold, relevant type generality, extent and frequency/propensity reading incompletely specified.
note: No statistical estimate, empirical process assessment or probability of a philosophical theory is supplied. Reliability is not identical to behavioral success or truth of one belief.
